top_story: Israel’s continued strikes in southern Lebanon, including the 9 September killing of 12 members of one family, show how ceasefire diplomacy is being hollowed out on the ground, sustaining fear, displacement, and pressure on already fragile border communities. In Gaza, reconstruction remains entangled with bombardment and coercive governance, leaving civilians trapped in a landscape where recovery efforts can reinforce wartime control rather than signal a real transition to peace. That persistent regional instability reached global energy infrastructure on 12 September when Saudi Arabia shut the East-West pipeline after drone attacks it attributed to Iraq, disrupting a route that carries up to 5 percent of world oil supply. The emerging picture is of conflicts that no longer stay local: violence is reshaping civilian life, political authority, and energy security across the region at once.
